plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three distinct strategy axes for a VIS-NIR dichroic beam splitter: (1) maximum layer count with quarter-wave initialization to exploit full manufacturing budget for band separation, (2) reduced layer count to test whether fewer layers with free optimization can match performance while improving manufacturability, and (3) non-quarter-wave thickness freedom to test whether deviating from classic DBR physics improves the transition sharpness at 45° incidence. All routes use TiO2/SiO2 on fused silica substrate at 45° incidence. The axes are genuinely distinct because they test different hypotheses about where the performance bottleneck lies: layer count, optimization freedom, or stack topology. Literature L01, L13, L15 directly motivate dichroic beam splitter design; L23 supports the optimization methodology; L32 addresses 45° incidence challenges.

routes.title: Maximum Layer Count Quarter-Wave DBR with Free Thickness Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer TiO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack initialized design, when thicknesses are freely optimized, will achieve higher visible reflectance and NIR transmittance than designs with fewer layers, because more interfaces provide greater spectral selectivity.
routes.design_principle: Distributed Bragg reflector physics: alternating high/low index layers at quarter-wave optical thickness create constructive interference for reflection in the stopband. More pairs deepen and widen the stopband. At 45° incidence, the effective optical thickness shifts, requiring thickness compensation.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (TiO2 | SiO2) × 12 | Fused Silica Substrate - 24 layers total, starting with TiO2
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers
manufacturing_considerations: 24 layers is the maximum allowed per requirement
TiO2 and SiO2 are standard evaporatable/sputterable materials
thickness tolerance sensitivity should be evaluated
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
expected_advantages: Maximum number of interfaces for spectral discrimination
Literature precedent for VIS-NIR beam splitters using this approach
known_risks: 45° incidence causes polarization splitting between S and P states
Thick stacks may accumulate stress and adhesion issues
Optimizer may converge to local minima with 48 thickness variables

Stack sequence: TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao) (24 layers total, starting with TiO2 (Siefke) adjacent to air). Materials: TiO2 (Siefke) and SiO2 (Gao) from catalogue. Substrate: SiO2 (Gao) (fused silica). Incident medium: air. Wavelength bands: 450-650 nm (target high reflectance), 700-1000 nm (target high transmittance). Angle: 45 degrees. Design variables: all 24 layer thicknesses in nanometers. Initialize thicknesses near quarter-wave optical thickness at 675 nm center wavelength, then optimize all thicknesses to maximize the composite objective. Maximum 24 layers constraint is satisfied exactly.

routes.title: Reduced Layer Count with Enhanced Thickness Freedom
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An 18-layer TiO2/SiO2 stack with fully free thickness optimization can match or exceed the performance of a 24-layer quarter-wave-initialized design, because optimization freedom compensates for reduced interface count.
routes.design_principle: Non-quarter-wave stacks can achieve similar spectral selectivity with fewer layers if thicknesses are optimized globally rather than constrained to quarter-wave values. This tests whether layer count or thickness optimization freedom is the dominant factor.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (TiO2 | SiO2) × 9 | Fused Silica Substrate - 18 layers total, starting with TiO2
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 18 layers
manufacturing_considerations: 18 layers reduces deposition time and stress compared to 24 layers
Fewer interfaces may improve yield and adhesion
Thickness tolerance requirements may be tighter with fewer layers
expected_advantages: Tests whether optimization can compensate for fewer layers
known_risks: May not achieve same band separation as 24-layer design
Optimization landscape may be more complex without quarter-wave initialization
Polarization splitting at 45° may be harder to manage with fewer degrees of freedom

routes.title: Edge-Transition Optimized Stack with Asymmetric Layer Pairing
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An asymmetric stack with more TiO2 layers than SiO2 layers, optimized for the 650-700 nm transition region, will reduce crosstalk better than symmetric quarter-wave stacks because the edge sharpness depends on index contrast distribution.
routes.design_principle: Dichroic edge filters benefit from asymmetric index profiles that steepen the transition. Placing more high-index layers near the transition region can sharpen the edge. This tests whether layer asymmetry improves band isolation.

known_risks: Asymmetric stacks may be more sensitive to thickness errors

Materials: TiO2 (Siefke) and SiO2 (Gao) from catalogue. Substrate: SiO2 (Gao) (fused silica). Incident medium: air. Wavelength bands: 450-650 nm (target high reflectance), 700-1000 nm (target high transmittance). Angle: 45 degrees. Design variables: all 22 layer thicknesses in nanometers. Initialize thicknesses with emphasis on transition region layers, then optimize all thicknesses. Maximum 24 layers constraint is satisfied.

routes.title: Quarter-wave TiO2/SiO2 dichroic stack with thickness tuning
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer periodic TiO2/SiO2 stack with quarter-wave optical thickness centered at approximately 550 nm will achieve high reflectance in 450-650 nm and high transmittance in 700-1000 nm at 45 degrees incidence, with the band-edge transition sharpness improving as layer thicknesses are optimized away from nominal quarter-wave values.
routes.design_principle: Bragg reflection from a periodic high-low index stack creates a photonic stopband centered at the quarter-wave condition. The stopband width scales with the index contrast (TiO2 ~2.4, SiO2 ~1.46). At oblique incidence, the effective optical thickness decreases by cos(theta_internal), shifting the stopband to shorter wavelengths. Unpolarized performance requires balancing s and p polarization responses.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica Substrate (24 layers total, 12 HL pairs)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers (d_TiO2_1 through d_TiO2_12, d_SiO2_1 through d_SiO2_12)
soft_objectives: maximize average reflectance in 450-650 nm band
maximize average transmittance in 700-1000 nm band
maintain smooth spectral transition without oscillations in passband
manufacturing_considerations: 24 layers is within typical deposition capability for ion-assisted evaporation or sputtering
TiO2 layers may have higher stress than SiO2 - alternating structure helps balance
thickness tolerance of ±2 nm typical for production - design should be robust to this
45-degree incidence requires angle-compensated thicknesses relative to normal-incidence quarter-wave
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack reflectance increases with number of pairs and index contrast
Stopband center wavelength shifts to shorter values at oblique incidence due to reduced effective optical path
S-polarization has higher reflectance than p-polarization at oblique incidence for dielectric stacks
Band-edge sharpness improves with more layers but saturates beyond ~10 pairs for high index contrast
Second-order reflection band appears at approximately half the center wavelength, should not interfere with NIR passband
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is well-understood and manufacturable
TiO2/SiO2 pair provides high index contrast (~2.4/1.46) for wide stopband
24 layers provides sufficient pairs for >95% peak reflectance in visible
Quarter-wave starting point gives good initial guess for optimization
known_risks: Uncertain whether 12 pairs is optimal vs fewer pairs with matching layers - did not check literature for pair-count optimization
Exact TiO2 refractive index dispersion in 450-1000 nm range is recalled approximately, actual dataset may differ
Polarization splitting at 45 degrees may cause visible-band reflectance to differ between s and p - user did not specify polarization state, assumed unpolarized average
Band-edge position may not align perfectly with 650/700 nm boundary without thickness tuning - this is what optimization addresses
Fused silica substrate refractive index (~1.46) is close to SiO2 coating index, which may affect first-layer impedance matching - did not verify exact substrate dataset
What would settle these: look up material_catalog dispersion data for tio2 and sio2, check substrate index, run polarization-resolved simulation
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar dielectric coating on fused silica substrate. Stack sequence from incident side: TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao) (12 alternating pairs). Materials: TiO2 (Siefke) (high index), SiO2 (Gao) (low index). Substrate: fused silica. Incident medium: air. Optimize all 24 individual layer thicknesses. Wavelength bands: 450-650 nm (target high reflectance), 700-1000 nm (target high transmittance). Incidence angle: 45 degrees. Polarization: unpolarized (average of s and p). Maximum layers: 24 (fixed). Objective: maximize visible reflectance while maximizing NIR transmittance, minimizing crosstalk between bands.

research_influence: L01 (Design And Fabrication Of Multilayer Dichroic Beam Splitter) directly motivates the dichroic beam splitter approach and validates TiO2/SiO2 as a viable material pair for this application
L13 (High rejection VNIR-SWIR beam splitter for Sentinel 2) provides precedent for VIS-NIR separation in imaging applications, supporting the band specification
L15 (Manufacturing of high performance VIS-NIR beam splitters) confirms manufacturability of this class of filters and informs the layer count constraints
L23 (Guaranteed global optimization of thin-film optical systems) supports the optimization methodology used across all routes
L38 (Exact and numerical design of non-polarizing edge filters) informs route_03's asymmetric edge optimization approach
L32 (Low Group Delay Dispersion Optical Coating at 45° Incidence) highlights the 45° incidence challenge that all routes must address
unresolved_decisions: Polarization state is not specified in the original request; all routes optimize for unpolarized or average performance, but S/P splitting at 45° may require post-optimization analysis
Incident medium is not explicitly stated; air is assumed as standard convention but should be confirmed
Fused silica substrate is represented as sio2 in the material catalogue; the registry resolution should confirm this matches the intended substrate optical properties
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all three routes fail to achieve best_target_score above 0.6 after full optimization, the fundamental constraint set (45° incidence, TiO2/SiO2 only, 24 layers max) may be insufficient for the specified band separation. Consider relaxing layer count, changing materials, or accepting reduced performance.

errors: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.

catalog.coverage: the guaranteed-name list proves name resolution only; the separate route candidate ranking reads actual n/k grids and records native coverage or explicit interpolation/endpoint-extension availability. Execution still keeps the registry's allow_extrapolation switch fail-closed

selector_payload.selection_rule: Candidates are pre-ranked by three equal physical metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1 is the most physically reliable candidate. Use the highest-ranked candidate that also satisfies the user's exact material formula, state and source constraints. Never replace SiO with SiO2 or another stoichiometry.

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests a quarter-wave Bragg stack design for visible-NIR dichroic splitting, drawn from recalled thin-film optics practice. The hypothesis is that a 24-layer TiO2/SiO2 periodic stack with quarter-wave optical thickness centered near 550 nm will produce high visible reflectance and high NIR transmittance at 45 degrees. I would have wanted to look up: exact dispersion data for TiO2 and SiO2 in the 450-1000 nm range, typical deposition stress limits for 24-layer stacks, and published dichroic designs for comparison of band-edge sharpness.

routes.title: Quarter-wave TiO2/SiO2 dichroic stack with thickness tuning
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer periodic TiO2/SiO2 stack with quarter-wave optical thickness centered at approximately 550 nm will achieve high reflectance in 450-650 nm and high transmittance in 700-1000 nm at 45 degrees incidence, with the band-edge transition sharpness improving as layer thicknesses are optimized away from nominal quarter-wave values.
routes.design_principle: Bragg reflection from a periodic high-low index stack creates a photonic stopband centered at the quarter-wave condition. The stopband width scales with the index contrast (TiO2 ~2.4, SiO2 ~1.46). At oblique incidence, the effective optical thickness decreases by cos(theta_internal), shifting the stopband to shorter wavelengths. Unpolarized performance requires balancing s and p polarization responses.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica Substrate (24 layers total, 12 HL pairs)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers (d_TiO2_1 through d_TiO2_12, d_SiO2_1 through d_SiO2_12)
soft_objectives: maximize average reflectance in 450-650 nm band
maximize average transmittance in 700-1000 nm band
maintain smooth spectral transition without oscillations in passband
manufacturing_considerations: 24 layers is within typical deposition capability for ion-assisted evaporation or sputtering
TiO2 layers may have higher stress than SiO2 - alternating structure helps balance
thickness tolerance of ±2 nm typical for production - design should be robust to this
45-degree incidence requires angle-compensated thicknesses relative to normal-incidence quarter-wave
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack reflectance increases with number of pairs and index contrast
Stopband center wavelength shifts to shorter values at oblique incidence due to reduced effective optical path
S-polarization has higher reflectance than p-polarization at oblique incidence for dielectric stacks
Band-edge sharpness improves with more layers but saturates beyond ~10 pairs for high index contrast
Second-order reflection band appears at approximately half the center wavelength, should not interfere with NIR passband
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is well-understood and manufacturable
TiO2/SiO2 pair provides high index contrast (~2.4/1.46) for wide stopband
24 layers provides sufficient pairs for >95% peak reflectance in visible
Quarter-wave starting point gives good initial guess for optimization
known_risks: Uncertain whether 12 pairs is optimal vs fewer pairs with matching layers - did not check literature for pair-count optimization
Exact TiO2 refractive index dispersion in 450-1000 nm range is recalled approximately, actual dataset may differ
Polarization splitting at 45 degrees may cause visible-band reflectance to differ between s and p - user did not specify polarization state, assumed unpolarized average
Band-edge position may not align perfectly with 650/700 nm boundary without thickness tuning - this is what optimization addresses
Fused silica substrate refractive index (~1.46) is close to SiO2 coating index, which may affect first-layer impedance matching - did not verify exact substrate dataset
What would settle these: look up material_catalog dispersion data for tio2 and sio2, check substrate index, run polarization-resolved simulation
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar dielectric coating on fused silica substrate. Stack sequence from incident side: TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao) (12 alternating pairs). Materials: TiO2 (Siefke) (high index), SiO2 (Gao) (low index). Substrate: fused silica. Incident medium: air. Optimize all 24 individual layer thicknesses. Wavelength bands: 450-650 nm (target high reflectance), 700-1000 nm (target high transmittance). Incidence angle: 45 degrees. Polarization: unpolarized (average of s and p). Maximum layers: 24 (fixed). Objective: maximize visible reflectance while maximizing NIR transmittance, minimizing crosstalk between bands.
